guidelines.start:
## Start here

Read this page, then Guidelines, before building anything from this file. Rules marked Lattice are specific to Lattice; everything else carries to a new product.

### What this file is

The design system for Lattice and anything built beside it: the app, the website, and new software another agent builds from it. It captures the app as it ships; improvements arrive through comments, one at a time.

- Paper is the source of truth. The copy in the Lattice repository (design-system/) is exported from here and never edited by hand.
- Pages: Foundations (colour, type, space, radius, elevation, motion, icons), Components (each at real geometry with its states), Patterns (empty, loading, error, forms, Settings) and Guidelines (these rules).
- Every value on the canvas is a design token. Use the tokens, never the hex or pixel value they hold.

### Tokens

Tailwind v4 namespaces: --color-*, --spacing-*, --container-*, --breakpoint-*, --opacity-*, --font-*, --font-weight-*, --text-*, --leading-*, --tracking-*, --radius-*.

- Paper has no light and dark modes, so a colour has two tokens: --color-name for light and --color-dark-name for dark. Build both themes from the same names.
- **[Lattice]** A token’s description names the app variable it mirrors (app: --surface-chrome). The drift check compares them.
- Font tokens hold the face Paper can draw; the full fallback stack is in the description after stack: and is what the export writes.
- Durations, easing curves and shadows have no Paper token type. They live in the spec:motion and spec:shadow blocks on Foundations → Motion, elevation, borders, icons, and the export turns them into tokens.

### Working loop

Comment in Paper, fix, update the system, then build new work from it.

- Leave a comment on the node that is wrong. An agent reads open threads through the Paper MCP (list_comment_threads, get_comment_thread), fixes the app and this file together, re-exports, and resolves the thread.
- **[Lattice]** Change a value here first, then in the app. The drift check fails until both agree.
guidelines.rules:
## Guidelines

When to use what, what never to do, and the contrast every surface owes its text. Rules marked Lattice are specific to Lattice; the rest are written to carry to a new product.

### Principles

- Compact chrome around comfortable reading and writing surfaces. Density is a property of the surface, not of the product.
- One of each: one accent, one serif voice, one focus ring, one elevation ladder, one motion system. A second of anything is a missing decision.
- State runs one way: hover is lighter than pressed, and hover lighter than selected lighter than active, so two states never read the same.
- Colour carries meaning, not decoration: status, the accent and file kinds. Everything else is ink on neutral surfaces.

### Colour

Surfaces, two inks, one accent, four statuses.

- Three neutral surfaces: the chrome is the ground (titlebar gutters and navigation), the sheet holds panels, editors and fields, and the lift holds everything that floats.
- Two inks only. Text is primary or secondary. A status colour belongs to an icon or a state, never to a third grey.
- Contrast: body text and every accent used as text reach 4.5:1 on every surface they stand on (the accent presets clear 4.6:1); secondary text clears 5.5:1 on the chrome; icons, file glyphs and control edges clear 3:1.
- **[Lattice]** The accent is neutral (Graphite) by default. A preset or custom accent also becomes the focus ring; the editor’s current line stays neutral under any accent.
- Status colours mean success, warning, danger and info. They are never substitutes for the accent.
- Never put a fixed light-theme hex in a reusable component; take the semantic token so dark follows.
- **[Lattice]** Tints (Paper, Sage, Mist, Dusk) move only the neutral surfaces to one hue: chrome takes the full tint, panels 70%. Text and lines stay neutral.
- **[Lattice]** The mark’s weft (blue) and warp (teal) are identity: the logo and one accent stroke of an illustration, never a control.

### Typography

Six roles, each a size with its own leading. Take both.

- Display 30/36 and Title 18/24 are the serif voice at regular weight, for titles only. Everything else is the interface font: Subtitle 13/18 semibold, Body 13/20, Caption 12/16, Micro 11/14 medium.
- Body compact (12/16 medium) is the text inside a control. A compact (28px) control drops to caption size.
- Typeset (14/22) is prose: long-form reading and the source editor. Code and diffs stay on the editor font.
- Nothing in the interface is set below 11px; metadata is 12px.
- Chinese sets in PingFang SC; a serif title falls to Songti SC, so it stays a serif in either language.
- A region that is read rather than scanned (Settings) runs every role one step up; Display does not step up.
- **[Lattice]** Release builds set Timeless Sans and Serif first. Those fonts never ship outside the app: the repository and public pages use the open faces.

### Space and geometry

- A 2px grid; layout lands on its 4px steps. 2 and 6 are for distances inside a control.
- Controls stand on two heights: compact 28px (dense chrome, toolbars, popover forms) and default 32px (forms, dialogs, Settings). Width belongs to the layout.
- Radius has four steps and the pill: 4 for a chip, 6 for anything a pointer lands on, 10 for a surface, 14 for a dialog. Pick a step, never a value between.
- A surface nested flush in another takes the outer radius less the inset, so the curves stay parallel.
- A pointer target is at least 24px, however small the control is painted.
- **[Lattice]** The titlebar and every panel tab strip are 40px; tabs stand on the compact height 6px in.

### Elevation

- One ladder: page, panel, raised, popover, floating, dialog. Menus and tooltips are popovers; toasts and drawers float; modals are dialogs.
- A floating surface stands on the lift with a ring for its edge and the level’s shadow. It never adds a border on top of the ring.
- A level’s shadow does not change with nesting. Shadows deepen in dark, where a faint one disappears.

### States and focus

- Hover is 5% of the ink, pressed 8%, a selected row 8% with medium weight; the darker chrome hovers at 6%.
- Keyboard focus is one ring, 2px at a 2px offset in the focus colour. Components never add a second ring, and pointer focus draws none.
- Text entry answers focus with its border, not the ring. Selection is a fill, never an outline.
- A disabled Button keeps a faint slab with stepped-back ink; icon buttons, switches and checkboxes fade to 42%.

### Motion

- Three spring tiers: fast 80 ms (hover, focus, fades), moderate 160 ms (menus, popovers, switches, rows), slow 240 ms with a small bounce (dialogs, drawers, panes). The bigger the thing, the slower the tier.
- Exits are one tier quicker and plain ease-out tweens, so a dismissal reads as final.
- Take a tier whole, duration and curve together. Off-tier moments are draw (560 ms) and flourish (720 ms), each played once.
- Animate transform, opacity and stroke-dashoffset only. Nothing animates in the writing surface. Under reduced motion a one-shot finishes at once.

### Icons

- Lucide line glyphs: 14px in the chrome, 16px on a default control or a dialog or toast mark, 12px in a meta row or beside a label as a chevron.
- A 1.5 stroke beside regular-weight text (menus) and 2 where an icon stands alone.
- Secondary ink at rest, primary when on, hovered or current. Colour is for status, the accent and file glyphs.
- **[Lattice]** A file glyph is one icon per kind, a page for what you write and an object for what you collect, stroked in its hue over a 16% tint (20% in dark).

### Which component

- Button: primary is the one answer of a dialog (at most one dark slab per dialog); tinted leads everywhere else; secondary is the default; ghost dismisses; danger confirms what destroys.
- Checkbox for an immediate choice inside a form; Switch for a persistent setting that applies on its own.
- Select for a value from a list; SegmentedControl for two to four mutually exclusive views; tabs for sections.
- Every notification is a toast. A reversible action happens at once and its toast offers Undo; confirm only what cannot be undone.
- A small dialog has one anatomy: serif title, one line of copy, fields 12px apart, actions 24px below. A 36px mark only when it asks something risky. Escape, the backdrop and Cancel close it; it draws no X.
- Panel and drawer headers close with an icon-only X with an accessible label.

### Copy

- Compact interface copy (titles, descriptions, empty states, helper text) ends without a full stop.
- Labels do the explaining. A control whose label needs a sentence under it gets a better label. No taglines, no eyebrows over titles in the product.
- Secondary copy only says what the writer would otherwise miss: why something is disabled, a warning before something irreversible, an error and its way out.
- A space before a unit (1.2 s), none before % (184%). Counts are grouped; in Chinese 万 and 亿 from 10,000.
- **[Lattice]** Shortcuts are drawn from the command table everywhere they appear, never typed beside a label.

### Empty, loading and error

- An empty region says what would be there in a short title and offers the next step. No paragraph explaining the feature.
- A load shows one indicator, and a quick one shows none: every indicator waits 150 ms. Where the view has a known shape, the indicator is a skeleton of it.
- An error names what failed and offers the way out; it fails alone and leaves the rest of the window working.
- An action asked for by name always answers, even when there is nothing to do.

### Never

- Never introduce a colour, size, radius, duration or shadow that is not a token. A second use of a raw value is a missing token.
- Never set text in a status colour to make it grey or quiet, and never use the accent as decoration.
- Never add a second focus ring, an outline for selection, or a border on a floating surface.
- Never use the serif for anything but titles, and never set interface text below 11px.
- Never animate layout, loop motion near the writing surface, or replay a moment on remount.
- **[Lattice]** Never style inside the embedded Agent (Synara) from the host; the bridge carries theme and accent.
- **[Lattice]** Never commit or publish the Timeless font files.
